request: why do we have leap years?

beats.intent: Bars of the leftover quarter day piling up over 4 years: 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1
beats.narration: A year is about three hundred and sixty five and a quarter days. Each year the extra quarter day piles up.
beats.code:
stage.title("Leap years")
bars = draw_bars(stage, [0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0], labels=["year 1", "year 2", "year 3", "year 4"])

beats.intent: The fourth bar, a whole day, lit
beats.narration: After four years the quarters make a whole day.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, bars[3], color=RED)
stage.caption("Four quarters make a day")

beats.intent: The bars beside 4 × 0.25 = 1 day, added as 29 February
beats.narration: So every fourth year gets an extra day, the twenty ninth of February.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"4 \times 0.25 = 1 \text{ day}")

request: why are time zones 15 degrees wide?

beats.intent: A circle for the Earth split into 24 equal slices
beats.narration: The Earth turns once, three hundred and sixty degrees, in twenty four hours.
beats.code:
stage.title("Time zones")
slices = VGroup(*[Sector(radius=2.2, angle=TAU / 24, start_angle=TAU * k / 24, color=BLUE if k % 2 else TEAL, fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1) for k in range(24)])
stage.play(FadeIn(slices))
stage.add(slices)

beats.intent: One slice lit with its angle of 15° marked
beats.narration: Split into twenty four hour-slices, each is fifteen degrees wide.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, slices[0], color=YELLOW)
stage.label(slices[0], "15°", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The circle beside 360° ÷ 24 = 15° per hour
beats.narration: Move fifteen degrees east and the sun rises an hour earlier.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"360^\circ \div 24 = 15^\circ \text{ per hour}")

request: how long does light take to reach the Moon?

beats.intent: The Earth and the Moon as circles 384,000 km apart
beats.narration: The Moon is about three hundred and eighty four thousand kilometres away.
beats.code:
stage.title("Light to the Moon")
earth = Circle(radius=0.6, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to(LEFT * 5)
moon = Circle(radius=0.2, color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to(RIGHT * 5)
stage.play(FadeIn(earth), FadeIn(moon))
stage.add(earth, moon)
br = Brace(Line(LEFT * 5, RIGHT * 5), DOWN)
stage.play(GrowFromCenter(br))
stage.add(br)
stage.label(br, "384 000 km", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: A flash of light travelling from the Earth to the Moon
beats.narration: Light covers three hundred thousand kilometres every second.
beats.code:
flash = Dot(earth.get_right(), color=YELLOW, radius=0.12)
stage.play(FadeIn(flash))
stage.play(flash.animate.move_to(moon.get_left()), run_time=1.3, rate_func=linear)

beats.intent: The trip beside 384000 / 300000 ≈ 1.3 seconds
beats.narration: So the trip takes about one point three seconds.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\frac{384\,000}{300\,000} \approx 1.3\ \text{s}")

request: why does crushed ice melt faster than a big cube?

beats.intent: A 2 by 2 square of ice with its outline, perimeter 8
beats.narration: Look at ice from the side: a two by two block has an outline of eight.
beats.code:
stage.title("Crushed ice melts faster")
big = Square(side_length=2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).shift(LEFT * 3)
stage.play(Create(big))
stage.add(big)
stage.label(big, "edge 8", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: The same ice split into four 1 by 1 squares spread apart, total edge 16
beats.narration: Break it into four small blocks: same amount of ice, but the edges add up to sixteen.
beats.code:
smalls = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=1, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(4)]).arrange_in_grid(2, 2, buff=0.4).shift(RIGHT * 3)
stage.play(TransformFromCopy(big, smalls))
stage.add(smalls)
stage.label(smalls, "edge 16", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: The blocks beside: same area, twice the surface
beats.narration: More surface touches the warm drink, so the crushed ice melts faster.
beats.code: stage.caption("Same ice, twice the surface")

request: why do elephants have thick legs? (the square-cube law)

beats.intent: Bars for a size doubled: strength (area) 4 times, weight (volume) 8 times
beats.narration: Double an animal's size. Its bones' strength depends on area, which grows four times; its weight on volume, which grows eight times.
beats.code:
stage.title("The square-cube law")
bars = draw_bars(stage, [1, 4, 8], labels=["size 1", "area ×4", "volume ×8"])

beats.intent: Fresh axes of size against area and volume, the volume curve pulling away
beats.narration: Keep scaling and weight outgrows strength faster and faster.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 4), y_range=(0, 64), labels=("scale", ""))
a = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda k: k ** 2, color=GREEN, label="k^2")
v = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda k: k ** 3, color=RED, label="k^3")
stage.caption("Green: strength (area). Red: weight (volume)")

beats.intent: The curves beside the ratio: weight per strength grows like k
beats.narration: So big animals need much thicker legs just to stand up.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\frac{k^3}{k^2} = k")

request: why do we always see the same side of the Moon?

beats.intent: The Earth in the middle and the Moon at four points of its orbit, a red mark on its near side
beats.narration: The Moon circles the Earth. Put a red mark on the side facing us.
beats.code:
stage.title("One face of the Moon")
earth = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8)
orbit = DashedVMobject(Circle(radius=2.5, color=GREY), num_dashes=40)
stage.play(FadeIn(earth), Create(orbit))
stage.add(earth, orbit)
moons = VGroup()
for a in (0, PI / 2, PI, 3 * PI / 2):
    c = 2.5 * np.array([np.cos(a), np.sin(a), 0])
    m = Circle(radius=0.3, color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to(c)
    mark = Dot(c - 0.3 * np.array([np.cos(a), np.sin(a), 0]), color=RED, radius=0.08)
    moons.add(VGroup(m, mark))
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(m) for m in moons], lag_ratio=0.3))
stage.add(moons)

beats.intent: The red mark facing the Earth at every position
beats.narration: At every point of the orbit the red mark still faces the Earth: the Moon turns once for each orbit.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, VGroup(*[m[1] for m in moons]), color=RED)
stage.caption("It spins once per orbit")

request: how do bicycle gears make you go faster?

beats.intent: A front gear of 40 teeth and a rear gear of 20 teeth joined by a chain
beats.narration: The pedals turn a front gear with forty teeth; the chain drives a rear gear with twenty.
beats.code:
stage.title("Bicycle gears")
front = Circle(radius=1.4, color=YELLOW).shift(LEFT * 2.5)
rear = Circle(radius=0.7, color=BLUE).shift(RIGHT * 2.5)
chain = VGroup(Line(front.get_top(), rear.get_top()), Line(front.get_bottom(), rear.get_bottom())).set_color(GREY_B)
stage.play(Create(front), Create(rear), Create(chain))
stage.add(front, rear, chain)
stage.label(front, "40 teeth", direction=DOWN, color=YELLOW)
stage.label(rear, "20 teeth", direction=DOWN, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: The front gear turning once while the rear gear turns twice, marks on each showing it
beats.narration: Turn the pedals once: forty teeth pass, which turns the small gear twice.
beats.code:
fm = Dot(front.get_top(), color=RED)
rm = Dot(rear.get_top(), color=RED)
stage.add(fm, rm)
stage.play(Rotate(fm, TAU, about_point=front.get_center()), Rotate(rm, 2 * TAU, about_point=rear.get_center()), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

beats.intent: The gears beside 40 / 20 = 2 wheel turns per pedal turn
beats.narration: The back wheel turns twice for every pedal turn: a gear ratio of two.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\frac{40}{20} = 2")
